result.title: Propose with the Gradient, Accept with the Loss: One Hedged Attack for Pixel-Sparse Robustness
result.summary: A pixel-sparse adversary may change a few pixels of an image to any value. Robustness to such attacks is currently measured with an ensemble, sparse-AutoAttack (sAA), because its members fail in different places: sparse projected gradient descent (sPGD) trusts a first-order model that a full pixel change breaks, and sparse random search (Sparse-RS) ignores the gradient even where it is informative. We show that both attacks are local searches, each a proposal distribution plus an acceptance rule, and ask what such a search can learn from the gradient. A Taylor bound says what to measure, and measurements at the states the search visits give five rules. The sign of the gradient is its most reliable use at a single pixel and sets a new pixel's value. Its ranking of candidate pixels should be followed loosely, and its ranking of the pixels to remove, which is often more reliable, can be followed more closely. A pixel should not be proposed twice before a move is accepted, and acceptance should be decided by the loss alone. These rules define Gradient-guided Random Search (GRS), which runs once and costs one forward and one backward pass per step. On 13 CIFAR-10 configurations and 5 ImageNet models, GRS matches or beats the best single member of sAA and is within one point of sAA itself or stronger on 17 of 18 settings, and it is significantly stronger than sAA on 8. It uses 3 instead of up to 7 forward-pass units, and on CIFAR-10 it runs 3.7 to 5.0 times faster than the members of sAA run in full.

AI.brief_summary: 论文把 sPGD 与 Sparse-RS 统一为「提议分布+接受规则」的局部搜索，依据 Taylor 界与搜索中实测给出五条梯度使用规则（符号定值、排序松跟随、接受只看损失等），据此提出单次运行的 GRS 像素稀疏攻击，在 CIFAR-10 与 ImageNet 上以更少前向与更快速度接近或超过 sAA。
AI.relevance_reason: 其将搜索拆为「梯度指引提议、仅用损失接受」的结构可供核查能否迁移到 latent 假设的提议与验证分工；对少数像素的选取与移除排序也可能类比视觉证据筛选与贡献分配。
